Route 1: Hydrothermal synthesis of Cu₂O  
1. Dissolve copper(II) nitrate trihydrate (Cu(NO₃)₂·3H₂O) (mass 2.0 g, approx. 0.012 mol) in deionized water (solvent volume 20.0 mL). Add ascorbic acid (mass 0.15 g, approx. 1.0 mmol) as a reducing agent and adjust the pH to 10.0 using 0.5 M NaOH solution (added volume ~5 mL). Transfer the solution to a Teflon‑lined autoclave, seal, and heat at 150 °C for 4 h. Cool the autoclave to room temperature, collect the precipitate by centrifugation, wash with water and ethanol, and dry at 60 °C.  
Final product: Cu₂O obtained as cubic crystals with a spherical morphology, average particle size ≈20 × 20 × 20 µm, corresponding to PDF reference 05‑0667.
